title: Water-Holding Capacity of Soils in the Steppe Zone of Northern Kazakhstan Under the Application of Superabsorbent Polymers
content: Soil moisture deficit limits agroecosystem stability and crop productivity in arid and semi-arid regions, including the steppe zone of Northern Kazakhstan. This study evaluated the effects of a synthetic superabsorbent polymer (SAP), agroperlite, and their composite application on water loss in soils with contrasting textures. Laboratory experiments were conducted using dark chestnut soil and ordinary chernozem represented by light, medium, and heavy loams. The first experiment compared SAP, agroperlite, and SAP + agroperlite based on total and average daily water loss. The second experiment evaluated the effects of SAP dosage for three particle-size fractions (100 mesh, 2.0–2.5 mm, and 5–10 mesh), whereas the third assessed the influence of SAP particle morphology on soil water retention. All amendments reduced water loss compared with the untreated control, but their effectiveness depended on soil texture. SAP was most effective in light and medium loams, whereas agroperlite and the SAP + agroperlite composite showed greater efficiency in heavy loams. Increasing SAP dosage consistently decreased water loss, with the strongest effect observed for the fine powder fraction (100 mesh). These results indicate that soil texture, application rate, and SAP particle morphology should be considered when selecting water-retaining amendments for moisture-deficit conditions.
